facts.text: On this date in 1999, a total solar eclipse crossed Europe from Cornwall to Istanbul — the last one visible from Paris until 2081, meaning almost no living Parisian will see another from their city.
On August 11, 1960, Chad declared independence from France, becoming one of 17 African nations to do so that single year — a pace of decolonization the world has never seen before or since.
Mongolia has a lower population density than any other sovereign nation on Earth: roughly 2 people per square kilometer, less than the open ocean averages in maritime traffic.
The Philippines is the only country where annulment, not divorce, is the standard legal remedy for failed marriages — a distinction it now shares only with Vatican City.
More people live within a 4,000-kilometer radius centered on Bangladesh than outside it — that circle, covering South and Southeast Asia, contains over half the entire human population.
On August 11, 1999, the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed above 11,000 for the first time — then spent the next three years giving most of it back as the dot-com bubble collapsed.
On August 11, 1971, Nixon's Treasury Secretary John Connally told G10 finance ministers: 'The dollar is our currency, but it's your problem.' The float era had begun.
The S&P 500 has spent roughly 75% of its history below its all-time high. The feeling of 'missing out' is, statistically, the normal condition of investing.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A share has never been split. At over $700,000 per share, it is the highest-priced stock on any major exchange — by design.
The entire Dutch East India Company, at its 1637 peak, was worth roughly $8 trillion in today's dollars — more than Apple, Microsoft, and Saudi Aramco combined.
On this date in 1999, the last total solar eclipse of the millennium crossed Europe. The Moon's shadow moves at 1,700 mph — faster than a rifle bullet.
Your skeleton is not static. Every 10 years, your entire bone mass is silently replaced, atom by atom, by osteoclasts and osteoblasts working in concert.
On this date in 1984, Reagan joked on a hot mic that he had 'signed legislation that will outlaw Russia.' Soviet military forces briefly went on alert.
A neutron star teaspoon weighs roughly a billion tons. Its surface gravity is 200 billion times stronger than Earth's, strong enough to bend light around its own crust.
Trees in a forest share sugars through fungal networks connecting their roots. A single Douglas fir can be linked to hundreds of neighbors simultaneously.
On this day in 1934, the first prisoners arrived at Alcatraz — a federal penitentiary that operated for fewer years (29) than the Golden Gate Bridge has been standing since Alcatraz closed.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramids are that old.
On this day in 1965, the Watts Uprising began in Los Angeles — six days of revolt that killed 34 people and remain less discussed than the 1 death at Woodstock four years later.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. Europe had medieval universities while Tenochtitlan was still unbuilt marshland.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before the telephone. Alexander Bain's electric printing telegraph could transmit images before anyone could transmit voice.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved that may never return. Linguists consider it untranslatable — the word itself enacts what it describes.
Hiraeth (Welsh): homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. It folds grief, nostalgia, and yearning into a single syllable cluster English cannot match.
Mamihlapinatapai (Yaghan): the look shared between two people who both want something but neither will initiate. Possibly the most meaning packed per letter of any word on record.
On this day in 1984, the Oxford English Dictionary first cited 'yuppie' in formal print — a word so precisely pegged to its moment that it became its own definition of obsolescence.
Forelsket (Norwegian): the euphoric vertigo of falling in love, before doubt arrives. English borrowed 'falling' for the experience but never found a word for what the fall feels like.
On this date in 2010, Laszlo Hanyecz made the first documented real-world Bitcoin purchase — two pizzas for 10,000 BTC. Those coins would peak at roughly $690 million in 2021.
On Aug 11, 2017, Bitcoin Cash completed its first difficulty adjustment after the fork, dropping mining difficulty by 20% to stabilize block production following the chain split.
Ethereum's EIP-1559, introduced in August 2021, has permanently burned over 4.5 million ETH to date — removing it from circulation via a base fee destroyed with every transaction.
Bitcoin's timelock script opcode, CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, means coins can be mathematically frozen until a future block height — a commitment enforced by code, not counterparties.
The largest single Bitcoin transaction by value occurred in April 2020: 161,500 BTC moved in one output, worth ~$1.1B at the time, for a fee of less than $1.
On this date in 2011, IBM's Watson was being prepared for its Jeopardy! debut — it had memorized all of Wikipedia but had no internet access during the match.
On August 11, 2023, Llama 2 had already been downloaded over 30 million times within weeks of Meta releasing it, collapsing the assumption that frontier models required centralized infrastructure.
AlphaFold2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known proteome — in a database that took weeks to generate and would have required millennia of lab work.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed around 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity, roughly equivalent to the annual consumption of 4,500 average U.S. households.

The first neural network to beat humans at Go, AlphaGo, did so in 2016 using a technique — Monte Carlo Tree Search combined with policy networks — that its own designers couldn't fully explain move-by-move.
